title: Imaging and quantification of apical microvilli in the syncytial blastoderm of Drosophila embryos
protocol: Place a fresh sucrose-agar plate smeared with yeast paste on the mouth of a cage containing Canton-S flies.
Replace the cage at 25°C and collect the sucrose-agar plate after 2.5 h.
Pour deionized water into the plate and dissolve the yeast carefully without breaking the sucrose-agar layer.
Carefully pour the contents of the plate into a cell strainer to separate embryos from the solution.
Wash the embryos multiple times with deionized water to remove debris.
Pour 5–6 mL of 4% bleach into an empty Petri plate.
Immerse the cell strainer in bleach for 1–1.5 min to remove the chorion.
Avoid increased exposure to bleach as this may damage the embryos.
Observe the embryos under a stereomicroscope before adding bleach.
Soak the embryos in bleach for 1 min and observe again.
Wash the embryos thrice with deionized water.
Dry the embryos by placing the cell strainer on a piece of soft tissue.
Add 1 ml of n-heptane to a scintillation vial.
Carefully transfer the embryos into the scintillation vial containing n-heptane.
Add a 1:1 mixture of 4% PFA and n-heptane (1 ml each) to the scintillation vial.
Bring the 4% PFA solution to room temperature before adding to ensure efficient fixation.
Place the scintillation vial on a rocker at room temperature for 25 min.
Carefully remove and discard the 4% PFA layer from the solution in the scintillation vial.
Remove the n-heptane.
Add fresh n-heptane and incubate the embryos at 4°C for a minimum of 40 min.
Cut rectangular pieces of double-sided tape (∼6 cm long) and Whatman filter paper (∼6 cm long, as wide as the double-sided tape).
Remove the plastic covering from one side of the tape and stick it to a 60 mm Petri plate along its diameter.
Transfer the embryos and n-heptane using a 200 μL pipette onto the filter paper rectangle.
Allow the n-heptane to evaporate, leaving the embryos on the filter paper.
Remove the plastic covering from the exposed surface of the tape.
Invert the filter paper rectangle such that the embryos face downwards.
Touch the inverted filter paper lightly on the sticky surface of the tape.
Pour enough 1× PBS into the Petri plate containing the immobilized embryos to submerge them.
Place the Petri plate under a stereomicroscope.
Poke each embryo at one end of its long axis with a 1 mL insulin syringe needle to rupture its vitelline envelope.
Give a slight push to each embryo with the needle to release it from its vitelline envelope.
Transfer de-vitellinized embryos in 1× PBS solution into a 0.6 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Remove the 1× PBS from the microcentrifuge tube containing de-vitellinized embryos without disturbing them.
Add 300 μL of 0.3% PBST to the tube containing the embryos.
Wash the embryos in 0.3% PBST for 5 min by placing the tube on a rocker at room temperature.
Allow the tube to stand for the embryos to settle at the bottom.
Using a 200 μL pipette, remove 0.3% PBST carefully without disturbing the embryos.
Add 300 μL of fresh 0.3% PBST and repeat the wash step twice more for a total of 3 washes.
Remove the 0.3% PBST after the last wash.
Add 300 μL of 2% PBTA to the tube.
Incubate the tube on a rocker at room temperature for 1 hour for the blocking process.
Allow the tube to stand so that the embryos settle at the bottom.
Using a 200 μL pipette, remove the 2% PBTA carefully without disturbing the embryos.
Dilute the primary antibody in fresh 2% PBTA (1:200 for Phospho-Histone H3 in rabbit).
Remove the 2% PBTA used for the blocking step and add the diluted primary antibody solution to the tube containing the embryos.
Incubate on a rocker at 4°C for a minimum of 16 hours.
Allow the tube to stand so that the embryos settle at the bottom.
Using a 200 μL pipette, remove the primary antibody solution carefully without disturbing the embryos.
Add 300 μL of fresh 0.3% PBST to the tube.
Place the tube on a rocker at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Repeat the wash step twice more for a total of 3 washes.
Dilute Alexa 488 phalloidin (1:100) and Alexa 568-coupled anti-rabbit secondary antibody (1:1,000) in 300 μL of 0.3% PBST.
Allow the tube to stand so that the embryos settle at the bottom.
Using a 200 μL pipette, remove the 0.3% PBST carefully without disturbing the embryos.
Add the secondary antibody/dye solution to the tube.
Wrap the microcentrifuge tube in aluminum foil.
Incubate the tube on a rocker at room temperature for 1 hour.
Thaw an aliquot of Mowiol-DABCO on ice.
Allow the tube containing the embryos to stand so that the embryos settle at the bottom.
Remove the secondary antibody/dye solution carefully without disturbing the embryos using a 200 μL pipette.
Add 300 μL of fresh 0.3% PBST to the tube.
Place the tube on a rocker at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Allow the tube to stand so that the embryos settle at the bottom.
Remove the 0.3% PBST carefully without disturbing the embryos using a 200 μL pipette.
Repeat this wash step twice more for a total of three washes.
After removing the 0.3% PBST from the final wash, add 100 μL of fresh 0.3% PBST to the tube.
Transfer the solution with embryos onto a glass slide.
Drain the excess 0.3% PBST by standing the slide on its side.
Space the embryos on the slide by gently pushing them apart from each other using a fine brush.
Drain out excess liquid using a thin piece of Whatman filter paper by dabbing the paper lightly at the edges of each embryo.
Using a cut 1 mL pipette tip, add two drops of Mowiol-DABCO solution to the slide.
Place a 22 × 40 mm, #1.5 coverslip on the slide carefully to avoid air bubbles.
Ensure that the Mowiol-DABCO solution covers the embryos completely.
Seal the edges of the coverslip with transparent nail polish.
Protect the slide from light by covering it with aluminum foil.
Allow the nail polish to set for 15 min at room temperature.
Store the slide in an opaque box at 4°C.
Image the slide within 1–2 days of preparation to minimize fluorophore signal degradation.
Mount the slide on the stage of an inverted TCS SP8 3× microscope with super-resolution STED module.
Load a 100×/1.4 NA oil immersion objective (refractive index 1.518).
Switch to fluorescence mode and toggle to the rhodamine/RHOD (red) filter.
Move the stage until an embryo becomes visible as an orange glow.
Use coarse and fine focus knobs to bring the surface of the embryo in focus.
Identify the mitotic stage of the syncytial division cycle based on phospho-histone H3 label.
Move through a few z-planes near the surface of the embryo and find an optical plane which has the greatest number of microvilli in focus.
Set the pinhole size to 1.00 AU.
Capture a standard confocal image using the standard mode with a zoom of 3.5× and scan speed 200 Hz.
Use the 592 nm pulsed depletion laser at 90% power in 2D STED mode for microvilli imaging.
Keep the gain at 100 and line averaging at 4.
Export images as 8 bit, 1024 × 1024 TIFF format with a pixel size of about 30–40 nm.
Deconvolve the images using the STED module on Huygens Professional version 17.04.
Estimate the average background using the In/near object module by controlling the radius parameter.
Use the Classical Maximum Likelihood Estimation (CMLE) algorithm and set the maximum iterations at 40.
Set the Signal to Noise Ratio at 7 and Quality Threshold at 0.1 in the ‘fast’ iteration mode with possible bleaching correction.
Save the deconvolved images as high-quality TIFF images.
